messages:
ana (support): heads-up: acme reported sudden p95 spike + intermittent 429s on their dedicated eu-west pool since ~03:00 UTC. started after an autoscale bump.

sam (eng-runtime): noted. did they hit any quota? can you paste the API error payload?

ana (support): payload: `HTTP 429, {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"reason\":\"unexpected_throttle\"}`. customer says requests queue then tail latency explodes. no recent config changes on their side.

mario (eng-infra): can we get node-level metrics from the pool? NVML, sm util, interrupts? rough hypothesis: noisy neighbor on a shared host after fractional MIG packing changed during autoscale.

ana (support): attaching last 30s sample from customer host (they ran our quick-collect):
```
[2026-03-17T03:02:12Z] nvidia-smi: GPU 0 sm: 98% mem: 42% enc: 0% dec:0%
[2026-03-17T03:02:13Z] nvidia-smi: GPU 1 sm: 12% mem: 5%
[2026-03-17T03:02:14Z] dmesg: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU HANG detected
[2026-03-17T03:02:15Z] /var/log/redwood/runtime.log: kvcache_lock failed for tenant=acme, err=EAGAIN
```

sam (eng-runtime): that GPU hang + sm imbalance is suspicious. which MIG config is the pool using? fractional (1g/2g slices) or full device?

luis (eng-ml): acme has a mix of small-slice jobs and one heavy batch job that started when autoscale added more fractional slices. fractional packing can create pressure on L3/cache and cause SM thrashing, very visible in sm% spikes.

ana (support): customer: pool id eu-west-ded-41, tenant id acme-001. they say autoscale policy did a rapid scale from 8->16 slices at 02:58.

mario (eng-infra): pulling scheduling logs for eu-west-ded-41. also checking MIG topology assignments.

mario (eng-infra): quick grep: one host (node-77) shows 12 fractional slices placed (mix of 1g & 2g) plus two full partitions—packing mismatch. kernel shows repeated quantize_kern OOM warnings during the window.

sam (eng-runtime): try a repro: have customer run sustained token-gen with --concurrency 20 on a small-slice model while we watch that node. command I used:
```
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"small-slice-v1","input":"lorem ipsum"}' & done
```

ana (support): they ran it and reproduced 429s ~30s in. attaching the API timing: mean latency jumps from 80ms -> 3.2s p95, and 429 bursts start at ~30s.

luis (eng-ml): please capture `nv-smi dmon` and `perf top` during repro if possible. also get `curl -i` output for the 429 responses (headers include route/id).

mario (eng-infra): I see evictions and slot reshuffle during autoscale: the scheduler allowed fractional slices to be colocated with heavy work. evicting or migrating the heavy job off node-77 should reduce tail.

sam (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation: 1) isolate tenant to hosts with homogeneous MIG partitions (we can set affinity), or 2) increase autoscale cooldown to avoid immediate reshuffle, or 3) route acme to dedicated full-GPU nodes for heavy batch windows. which do we want to propose to customer now?

ana (support): customer prefers minimal change. they asked for a workaround without downtime.

mario (eng-infra): we can apply a soft-affinity to avoid node-77 for acme (no restart). also throttle per-tenant concurrency at the router for 10m to smooth load peaks. I'll open an infra task to migrate heavy pods off node-77 during the next maintenance window.

sam (eng-runtime): I can push a hotfix to the autoscaler: add a placement safety check to avoid colocating high-sm jobs with many fractional slices. low risk patch; will roll to canary.

luis (eng-ml): also recommend model-side change: switch to a slightly larger batchable variant for the heavy workload during peak windows; that'll reduce scheduling jitter and SM spikes.

ana (support): agreed. proposed immediate actions sent to customer: 1) we enable router concurrency cap at 12 for 10m, 2) we apply soft-affinity to steer them off node-77, 3) ops schedules migration for next maintenance, 4) eng-runtime will roll canary autoscaler fix. they accepted.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0423, priority P2, owners: eng-infra (mario), eng-runtime (sam).

mario (eng-infra): executed steer: `rbac routing set-affinity --pool eu-west-ded-41 --tenant acme-001 --avoid-host node-77` returned OK.

sam (eng-runtime): autoscaler patch queued; canary build id: canary-2026.3.17-11; will monitor first 30m.

ana (support): customer confirms immediate tail improvement after soft-affinity + concurrency cap: p95 down to 220ms, no further 429s for 15m. they still want a long-term fix to avoid reshuffle-induced noise.

luis (eng-ml): file a follow-up with model-recommendation doc and quant profiling. I'll own the eval.

mario (eng-infra): opening infra follow-up: ensure scheduler respects homogeneous-MIG placement when autoscale delta > 30% of pool.

sam (eng-runtime): will add unit/integration tests for the placement safety.

ana (support): thanks team. closing loop with customer and documenting repro steps + collected logs in the ticket. :white_check_mark:

mario (eng-infra): notes for postmortem: root cause = autoscale-induced fractional-packing reshuffle + a heavy unthrottled SM-hungry job colocated with many fractional MIG slices causing L3/SM thrash -> elevated latency and transient 429s from router backpressure. mitigations: affinity steering, router concurrency caps, autoscale placement safety check, and longer cooldowns.

sam (eng-runtime): tagging: #noisy-neighbor #mig #autoscale #dedicated-pool
